Fiber-reinforced reactive nano-epoxy composites include carbon, glass, aramid, and ultra-high-molecular-weight polyethylene (UHMWPE) fibers.
The nano-epoxy matrix in the fiber-reinforced composites has improved wetting, lower viscosity, and better rheological properties compared to pure epoxy.
The fiber-reinforced nano-epoxy composites showed 25% higher strength, 20% higher modulus, and 30% higher toughness compared to pure epoxy.
The metal-matrix/hollow-ceramic-sphere composites have a density less than that of beryllium (1.2-1.7 g/cm3 vs. 1.85 g/cm3) and a modulus as high as 25 Msi (170 GPa).
The hollow ceramic spheres in the metal-matrix composites have a low density of 0.5 g/cm3 and a high crush strength of 40-80 ksi (276-552 MPa).
The metal-matrix/hollow-ceramic-sphere composites can be tailored for properties like radiation shielding, EMI shielding, and thermal expansion control.
The metal-matrix/hollow-ceramic-sphere composites can be processed like metals through machining, joining, and coatings.
Piezoelectrically enhanced photocathodes use materials like AlxGa1-xN compounds to induce strain and create strong electric fields that enhance electron emission.
Piezoelectrically enhanced photocathodes could be used in devices like microchannel plates, electron-bombarded charge-coupled devices, image tubes, and night-vision goggles.
The iridium-doped ruthenium oxide catalyst is designed to be a durable and efficient catalyst for the electrolysis of water in polymer-electrolyte-membrane (PEM) fuel cells.
Doping ruthenium oxide with iridium helps stabilize it at the oxygen evolution potentials required for water electrolysis.
The piezoelectrically enhanced photocathodes would have similar electron-emission properties to cesiated photocathodes but would be stable in air, allowing for easier and lower-cost fabrication.
The metal-matrix/hollow-ceramic-sphere composites are intended to replace beryllium as a structural material in aerospace applications.
The iridium-doped ruthenium oxide catalyst could be used in the fabrication of water electrolysis units for hydrogen generators.
The fiber-reinforced nano-epoxy composites showed improved thermal properties including higher glass transition temperature (Tg) and more stable coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE).
